claims.text: This is not a distance dispute, and the rider has not made one: the driver's own trace measures the trip at 25.17 km against a 24.80 km booked optimal, an excess of 0.37 km, or 1.49%, which fails both POL-RD-01 gates (greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20%), so no deviation is established and POL-RD-02 has nothing to recompute. That does not close the rider's case: POL-RD-01 expressly preserves a billing-integrity correction on a charge line 'whether or not a deviation exists', and the whole of the rider's $5.00 contest is the single $5.00 ERP line on the fare ledger - not the base fare, the distance charge, the time charge or the platform fee, all of which she leaves standing.

One gantry crossing can carry only one metered cost. The driver's trace places the vehicle 0.0 m from the CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) gantry at 08:27:10 - exactly the timestamp the fare ledger records as the charge time - and the ledger bills one ERP line of $5.00, with off_optimal_route_total 0.00 and on_optimal_route_total 5.00. POL-RD-09(1) provides that a third-party or government-set pass-through charge is 'never counted twice', and POL-RD-09 licenses a PARTIAL_REFUND. On the rider's account she paid that same $5.00 in cash at the gantry, so the single metered cost has been collected twice - once by the driver in cash, once on the app bill - and the app's line is the only one of the two duplicates the platform can reverse.

The driver's own statement confirms the conversation the rider relies on: he says 'I said the fare doesn't include ERP', i.e. he told her before the trip that the ERP was not inside the fare, and he does not deny receiving the cash - he offers only that 'if she gave me cash that was her choice'. What he does deny, a second collection, is a denial that cites no artifact, and there is none for him to cite: the chat log for this trip carries zero messages and the trip record's chat_message_count is 0, so his denial has no documentary support. POL-RD-08 provides that an assertion citing no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded.

The record does not settle whether the $5.00 cash was handed over: the chat log is empty (0 messages, no first-message timestamp), the ledger records no cash line, no credit and no refund (refund_issued_sgd 0.0, payment_status CHARGED), and the rider's account is met only by the driver's uncited denial, so the deciding fact is carried by no artifact at all. Where the record genuinely cannot answer the question, the disputed amount should be held rather than collected: under POL-GEN-03 an ESCALATE holds the amount rather than collecting or refunding it, and with the deciding fact recorded nowhere there is nothing on which a confidence above the platform-wide 0.70 floor could rest under POL-RD-10(1) and POL-GEN-02. If the tribunal will not reverse the duplicated $5.00 line, it should hold it, not collect it.

The rider is not the repeat unsubstantiated claimant POL-RD-08 is aimed at: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the clause's enhanced-corroboration condition (4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated) is not met and her account attracts no extra corroboration requirement under that clause. No other field on either profile is relied on for any purpose, in accordance with POL-GEN-01.

The bundle carries one impaired artifact and the rider discloses it as POL-GEN-02(1) requires rather than presenting it as clean: EV-ADVIS-00522-01 is a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY with admissibility status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT - no advisory covers the optimal corridor in this window. Its absence is itself citable, and it means the bundle offers no road-condition explanation of any kind for the trip; the driver's only account of the duplicate is 'the app billed ERP as normal', which is precisely the rider's complaint. With no advisory on file, no external-traffic explanation can be run or carry weight under POL-RD-13.

claims.text: No route deviation exists on this trip's own trace. The GPS polyline measures 25.17 km against a booked optimal of 24.8 km, an excess of 0.37 km — 1.49%. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH establishment gates to pass: excess greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms AND greater than 20% of optimal. Neither passes, and the derived block itself records the status as 'no deviation'. POL-RD-01 is explicit that if either establishment test fails no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip, the only carve-out being a billing-integrity refund under POL-RD-09(4).

The single ERP line on this fare is placed by the trace itself, so POL-RD-09(4) has nothing to bite on. The charge is CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) at SGD 5.00, recorded at 2026-09-10T08:27:10+08:00; the GPS trace's nearest fix to that gantry's coordinates is 0.0 m away at that exact second (fix index 153), and the line is flagged on_optimal_route. POL-RD-09(4)'s full refund is confined to a gantry the trace never passes. This gantry was crossed, on the optimal corridor.

The payments ledger carries one and only one ERP charge for this trip: the ERP itemisation totals SGD 5.00, the on-optimal-route total is SGD 5.00, the off-optimal-route total is SGD 0.00, and there is exactly one itemised gantry line. Whatever may have passed in cash between the parties, no platform record shows a second ERP charge, so there is no duplicated ledger line for a tribunal to reverse.

The rider's account of an oral agreement to pay the ERP directly in cash rests on her claim text alone; no artifact in this bundle supports it. The in-app chat export for this trip contains zero messages (message_count 0, truncated false, first and last message timestamps null), so the corroborating chat record POL-RD-04 and POL-RD-08 both look to is simply empty. Under POL-RD-08 an assertion from either side that cites no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded — and the rider has cited no artifact for the cash payment she alleges.

I disclose the impairment of the bundle's only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00522-01: it is MISSING, carries no payload, weight_multiplier 0.0, and fired the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. Its absence is immaterial to this ruling, because the driver's position does not rest on any POL-RD-03 exoneration — with excess measured at 0.37 km there is no deviation to exonerate — and no party has asserted an external traffic cause (queue, closure, breakdown or incident) for this trip, so POL-RD-13's comparison of an asserted traffic excuse against the advisory is not engaged on either side.

No repeat-deviation pattern can be found against this driver, and POL-RD-06 is not even triggerable here. The clause is consulted only where POL-RD-01 records a MATERIAL deviation, and this trip records none; in any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 250, so neither the 3-flag test nor the 0.05 ratio test is met. The driver's other profile fields — acceptance rate, rating, account age, lifetime counters — are context only under POL-GEN-01 and are not relied on as a ground of decision, nor is his lifetime prior_deviation_flags, which POL-RD-06 expressly says is not the trailing-90-day figure it asks for.

No POL-RD-10 trigger fires, so there is nothing here for a human reviewer to resolve. The trace is complete — 247 fixes, 100% coverage, an empty gaps array, max_gap_sec 0.0 and no straight-line jump — so limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 are not met and the POL-RD-10(3) escalation route is closed; the trip identifier and timestamps agree across the trip record, the trace and the ledger; and the only line that could look unmatched, the SGD 5.00 ERP charge, is matched by a fix at 0.0 m at the charged second, so POL-RD-10(8) is not engaged. The rider's remedy, if any, lies in the fare ledger, and the ledger answers the question.

The outcome is NO_ACTION. On this rider-filed dispute the present state is payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00. With no deviation established under POL-RD-01, no billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4), and no artifact evidencing a second ERP charge, the filing party's claim is not supported by the evidence and the present state stands. POL-GEN-03 gives NO_ACTION exactly that party-relative meaning: on a rider-filed dispute it leaves the charge in place, and it never means restoring or creating a refund.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties' points are answered together where they cover the same ground.

No route deviation exists. The trace measures the trip at 25.17 km against the 24.80 km booked optimal — an excess of 0.37 km, or 1.49% — so neither POL-RD-01 gate (more than 0.8 km and more than 20%) is met, POL-RD-02 does not run, and no distance refund is due. The driver is right on that, and the rider does not dispute the distance.

The ERP line itself is genuine. The trace places the vehicle on the CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) gantry at 08:27:10 on 10 Sep 2026 — the exact second the ledger charges — at 0.0 m from the gantry and on the optimal route. So POL-RD-09(4) does not fire: the gantry was crossed, there is no phantom line, and no billing-integrity referral is produced. The driver is also right that the ledger bills only one ERP line: $5.00, inside a total charged of $39.98.

The duplicate is in cash, not on the ledger. The rider says the driver told her before the trip to pay the ERP to him and that she handed him $5.00 at the gantry. The driver's own statement confirms he told her 'the fare doesn't include ERP' and does not deny the cash — he says only that 'if she gave me cash that was her choice.' That is an admission against his own interest (a driver does not concede a payment that helps the rider unless it happened), and it is the evidence that carries this fact; it does not rest on the rider's word alone. The empty chat log (0 messages) therefore cuts against the driver, not the rider: nothing contradicts her, and his denial cites no artifact.

Under POL-RD-09 a government-set pass-through cost is never counted twice. The single $5.00 ERP was collected once in cash and once on the app bill, so the $5.00 billed again through the app is refunded. The figure is the ERP line read from the fare breakdown: total charged $39.98, ERP on the optimal route $5.00, off-optimal-route ERP $0.00. The whole of the $5.00 you contested is returned, but because the gantry crossing was real the correction is a pass-through refund of $5.00 under POL-RD-09 rather than an acceptance that the fare was wholly wrong.

On the rider's escalation argument: this record does decide the point. Because the driver's statement carries the cash fact as an admission, the deciding fact is not 'carried by no artifact,' so confidence does not fall below the 0.70 floor. Confidence is 0.80, capped by the weight-1.0 artifacts that carry the charges (the GPS trace and the fare ledger); the counterparty statement carries no weight multiplier and so neither raises nor lowers the cap.

The remaining points do not change the outcome. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the trace is complete (247 fixes, 100% coverage, 0.0 s maximum gap), so POL-RD-07 limbs (a)–(c) are not met; identifiers and timestamps agree; and the ERP line has a trace counterpart. No repeat-deviation pattern exists (driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 across 250 completed trips in 90 days) and POL-RD-06 is not triggered, because there is no material deviation and no pattern. The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00522-01, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) is immaterial — no party asserts an external traffic cause. The rider's profile is not used against her and attracts no enhanced corroboration. No clause in this case produces a referral, so none is made.

ruling.explanation:
Both sides agree on the arithmetic and the record confirms it. The GPS trace measures this trip at 25.17 km against a booked optimal route of 24.80 km — an excess of 0.37 km, or 1.49%. POL-RD-01 establishes a route deviation only where the excess is BOTH greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20% of the optimal distance. Neither gate is met, so no deviation exists, the outcome on the distance-and-time lines is NO_ACTION, and POL-RD-02 never runs. The refund block on the fare breakdown (recomputed_fare 37.44, refund 2.55) is therefore not payable and is not awarded.

The only ERP line in the ledger is the CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) gantry, SGD 5.00 charged at 08:27:10. The GPS trace passes within 0 metres of that gantry at that exact second and the line is recorded on the optimal route. That makes it a genuine pass-through, so POL-RD-09(4) — which refunds a gantry the trace NEVER passes — has nothing to correct, and POL-RD-09(1)'s 'never counted twice' rule has no second ledger line to reverse: the ledger shows one ERP charge (on_optimal_route_total 5.00, off_optimal_route_total 0.00) and no cash or duplicate entry.

The rider's account that she also handed the driver SGD 5.00 in cash is not recorded in any artifact. The in-app chat export for this trip is empty (0 messages, no first/last message timestamps), and the payments ledger carries no cash line. POL-RD-08 places the initial burden on the rider and provides that an assertion from either side which cites no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded; the cash allegation cites no artifact, so it cannot found a refund. The driver's statement denies that he charged twice. On this record the SGD 5.00 the app billed for a gantry the car actually crossed is a legitimate charge.

On the request to hold rather than collect: I have not escalated. The trace is complete — 247 fixes, 100% coverage, empty gaps array, max_gap_sec 0.0, no straight-line jump — so POL-RD-07(a)-(c) are not met and POL-RD-10(3) is closed. Trip identifiers and timestamps agree across the trip record, trace and ledger, so POL-RD-10(2) and (4) are not engaged. The one ERP line is matched by a fix at 0.0 m, so POL-RD-10(8) is not engaged, and no charge line is unmatched. The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00522-01 (weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT) is immaterial: no party asserted a traffic cause, so POL-RD-13 and POL-RD-03 are not in play, and its absence is disclosed rather than relied on. This claim is not left unanswered by the evidence; it is unsupported by it, and an unsupported claim is decided against the claimant rather than escalated.

No profile field decides anything. The driver's trailing-window counters (deviation_flags_90d 0 against completed_trips_90d 250) show no repeat pattern and POL-RD-06 is not triggerable without a MATERIAL deviation; the rider's deviation_claims_60d (0) and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated (0) do not raise the POL-RD-08 corroboration requirement. Ratings, account ages, lifetime counters, prior-dispute counts and prior_no_show/no_show_terminations figures appear on the profiles but are context only under POL-GEN-01 and are not used.

Outcome: NO_ACTION, the party-relative meaning under POL-GEN-03. The present state stands — payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00 — and the SGD 5.00 ERP line remains. If the rider believes a cash payment was taken at the gantry, that is a matter between her and the driver outside the platform's ledger; nothing in this policy makes the platform's own matched ERP charge refundable on the present record, and the rider is free to put that account to the platform's support team.

This is a $5.00 dispute filed by the rider over the ERP line on a Woodlands-to-Raffles-Place trip. Both parties are addressed below, and every surviving claim is answered.

It passes neither, so no deviation is established and the rider's own advocate is right that POL-RD-02 has nothing to recompute. The refund arithmetic on the fare ledger (charged_total $39.98 less a recomputed fare of $37.44, i.e. $2.55) is therefore not payable: POL-RD-02 runs only where a deviation is established. POL-RD-09(1), which the rider invokes, is a rule against counting the same ERP charge twice inside a refund computation — it is not a rule that a rider who pays twice is refunded, and it does not apply where no POL-RD-02 refund runs.

ERP line — matched, not duplicated. The ledger (EV-FARE-00522) carries exactly one ERP charge: $5.00 for CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) at 08:27:10, with on-optimal-route total $5.00 and off-optimal-route total $0.00. The trace places the vehicle 0.0 m from that gantry at that exact second (fix index 153), on the optimal corridor. POL-RD-09(4)'s billing-integrity refund is confined to a gantry the trace never passes or a surcharge wrongly applied; this gantry was crossed. There is no second ledger line to reverse, so the platform's single ERP charge is legitimate and stands.

The cash payment — unsupported. The rider says she handed the driver $5.00 in cash for the same ERP. No artifact carries that fact. The in-app chat for this trip (EV-CHAT-00522) is empty — 0 messages, null first/last timestamps — and the ledger records no cash line, no credit and no refund (refund_issued_sgd 0.00, payment_status CHARGED). POL-RD-08 places the initial burden on the rider and provides that an assertion citing no evidence ID carries no weight; her cash account cites none. The driver's counterparty statement does not fill the gap: it confirms he told her the fare does not include ERP, but it denies charging twice, records only that 'the app billed ERP as normal', and its 'if she gave me cash that was her choice' is a conditional, not an admission that he received it. That statement is evidence, but it carries no weight_multiplier, so it neither raises nor lowers the confidence cap.

Escalation — no trigger. The rider asks that the $5.00 be held rather than collected. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires. The trace is complete — 247 fixes, 100% coverage, empty gaps array, max gap 0.0 s, no jump — so POL-RD-07(a)-(c) are not met and the POL-RD-10(3) route is closed; the trip identifiers and timestamps agree across trip record, trace and ledger; the only charge line is matched to the trace, so POL-RD-10(8) is not engaged; no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing artifact (POL-RD-10(5)); and the ruling rests on weight-1.0 artifacts, so confidence sits above the 0.70 floor and POL-RD-10(1) is not engaged. An open question that the record cannot resolve is not itself an escalation.

Missing advisory. EV-ADVIS-00522-01 is a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY with status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue MISSING_ARTIFACT. Both sides disclosed it, as POL-GEN-02(1) requires. It is immaterial: no party asserts a queue, closure, breakdown or incident, so POL-RD-13's comparison is not engaged and there is no deviation for an advisory to excuse. Its weight is 0.0 and it carries no fact.

Profiles. No adverse finding is built on either profile. The driver's deviation record (deviation_flags_90d 0 over completed_trips_90d 250) fails both POL-RD-06 tests, and no material deviation exists, so POL-RD-06 is not triggered and no driver-conduct referral arises. The rider's counters (deviation_claims_60d 0, deviation_claims_60d_substantiated 0) mean POL-RD-08's enhanced-corroboration condition is not met, which changes nothing here. Rating, account age, lifetime counters and prior_deviation_flags were mentioned only; under POL-GEN-01 they are context only and nothing is decided on them, as both advocates correctly accepted.

Outcome. The rider's claim of a duplicated ERP charge is not supported by the evidence, so under POL-GEN-03 the outcome is NO_ACTION and the present state stands: payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd $0.00 is left as it is. No refund issues to the rider and no compensation is payable to the driver. The one thing this record cannot settle — whether cash actually changed hands between the parties off-platform — is a matter between them that the platform's single, matched ERP charge does not change; it belongs here as an open question, not in the referrals list, and the rider may pursue it through in-app support.
